objective.text: Acquire multiple row locks in a consistent order to avoid the stated deadlock cycle.

difficulty.rationale: Break the stated wait cycle by making all participants acquire the shared resources in the same order.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: PostgreSQL 18. Transfers lock two existing account rows one at a time with lockForUpdate inside a transaction. All transfer paths can follow the chosen rule.

stem: Transfer A locks account 4 then waits for 9. Transfer B locks 9 then waits for 4. Which change prevents this particular opposite-order cycle while retaining exclusive protection of both balances?

options.text: Increase the deadlock retry count but keep both acquisition orders unchanged.
options.rationale: Retries can recover failed attempts but do not prevent this ordering cycle from recurring.
options.misconception: Retries can recover failed attempts but do not prevent this ordering cycle from recurring.

options.text: Sort the two account IDs and acquire both row locks in ascending order in every transfer path.
options.rationale: A common resource order prevents one transfer holding 9 while waiting for 4 as another holds 4 and waits for 9. Other causes still warrant bounded retries.

options.text: Acquire the second lock after committing the first balance update.
options.rationale: This splits the protected transfer and sacrifices atomic protection of the two balances.
options.misconception: This splits the protected transfer and sacrifices atomic protection of the two balances.

options.text: Use the sender account first in every transfer, regardless of numeric order.
options.rationale: Opposite-direction transfers still start with different rows and recreate the described cycle.
options.misconception: Opposite-direction transfers still start with different rows and recreate the described cycle.

validation.reason: PostgreSQL documents consistent lock acquisition order as the principal defense against this wait cycle. Laravel supplies the locking query; no multi-connection PostgreSQL execution is claimed.
